We also found that silencing PinX1 combined with radioimmunotherapy dramatically promoted M1 macrophage polarization in NSCLC. We know that in lung cancer, macrophages are a major component of the TIME [51]. There are two main phenotypes of macrophages, pro-inflammatory (M1-type) macrophages and anti-inflammatory (M2-type) macrophages [52]. M1-type macrophages can kill tumor cells through mediating cytotoxicity directly or mediating antibody-dependent cytotoxicity, while pro-tumourigenic M2-type macrophages is committed to tumor growth, invasion and metastasis [52]. Therefore, reprogramming of tumor-associated macrophages from M2-type to M1-type is critical for alleviating the immunosuppressive state of the TIME and controlling tumor growth. Other than induced ICD, optimized radiation can also promote the conversion of M2 macrophages to M1 in the TIME [53]. These findings may explain why targeting PinX1 could improve the tumor-suppressive immune microenvironment.
